name: Benaiah
overview: Benaiah was a male Levite who served as the overseer of the consecrated things under Conaniah, indicating a leadership role in the sacred duties of the temple. His service is noted specifically in 2 Chronicles 31:13, highlighting his responsibility within the Levitical tribe. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Benaiah means 'YHWH has built,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning that acknowledges God's active role in his life. This proper name is attested in 2 Chronicles 31:13 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Benaiah as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe set apart for temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Benaiah's significance lies in his role as overseer of the consecrated things, a position that entrusted him with managing sacred temple responsibilities during the time of Conaniah. His Levitical heritage underscores the continuity of God's appointed order for worship and service. Though mentioned briefly, his role exemplifies faithful stewardship in the administration of temple affairs.
